metadata.title: 5-star Analyst Doubles Down On Palantir Stock After Event

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) is drawing another bullish Wall Street call despite weakness in the stock, with Baird analyst William Power reiterating an Outperform rating and $200 price target after a recent technology demonstration. Power argues Palantir is positioned to benefit from broader adoption of open-weight AI models, agentic AI and sovereign AI, strengthening the case that its growth opportunity extends well beyond traditional government analytics contracts.
Palantir builds software platforms that help governments and businesses integrate data, run analytics and deploy artificial intelligence into real-world operations. Its revenue comes from commercial customers as well as large government and defense contracts, with AI adoption increasingly driving growth across both businesses.
Power said the demonstration reinforced his confidence in Palantir's enterprise opportunity. We remain confident that PLTR is well positioned to improve/modernize operations for enterprises, Power wrote.
He also sees open-weight AI models creating another avenue for growth. We believe that the company can capitalize on the growing popularity of open weight models, Power said.
The optimism follows a powerful second quarter. Palantir's revenue surged 94% year over year to $1.94 billion, while U.S. government revenue jumped 90% to $809 million.
Defense could provide another catalyst. William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma recently reaffirmed a Buy rating and estimated Palantir's Maven Smart System could eventually approach $1 billion in annual recurring revenue.
Maven is Palantir's AI-powered military platform, and government contracts represented roughly 42% of Q2 revenue.
Investor Takeaway
For Palantir investors, the next major test is whether extraordinary revenue growth can remain durable as AI adoption expands.
Investors should watch commercial growth, government revenue, AI-platform adoption and Maven contract momentum. One potentially important near-term catalyst is Maven receiving program-of-record status from the Pentagon, expected by the end of the U.S. government fiscal year in September.
That designation could make funding more predictable and strengthen Palantir's defense revenue visibility. But after rapid growth and strong investor expectations, any slowdown in AI adoption or government contract momentum could put pressure on the stock's premium valuation.
